notes.title: Status Report: Working on New Research Mechanics, New Plans and Much More
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/6243493e07dbbe084673bac8ee717a2b3237e3b8.jpg[/img]

Ahoy, engineers!

The bad news is: no update is coming out this week. But we can explain!

This week, we're very busy working on a brand [b]new mechanics for researching[/b]. We don't want to spoil the surprise just yet, but here's a teaser: cat researchers will get their own Tavern (maybe even an Inn) at KOTOVOD, along with their own sets of skills. No, we're not planning to add any RPG elements (although who knows!), but the way we see it -- it's going to make researching new technologies more complicated and interesting.

We are hoping to deliver it to you next week! And as it usually is, the update will not be just about researching. Some new art and various improvements are definitely implied! Check out this fascinating fishing robot, for one: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/4427e11898e6866bd8a883e2bb130321aa2cf908.gif[/img]

We've also spent a good amount of time discussing future plans! The summary of our collective mindwork is this new and updated roadmap. Can you spot what's new?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/556700b9f7b67932f4265eb9d585170be52e6381.png[/img]

Ok, here's a hint: we've added stuff to Stages 1 & 2! There will be mini quests, more communication from cats and another machine learning model. In short, it's gonna be awesome! Stay tuned for more news :)

Finally, we want to share a short fun video, explaining how machine learning works at Learning Factory (in case you don't know that already somehow):

[previewyoutube=OE08k99KxBg;full][/previewyoutube]

That's it for today, but not for this week! We have another fun activity for the weekend for you, so make sure to come back tomorrow :) Until then, folks!

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #27: Update Today, Live Stream Tomorrow!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/6196e409347e8c03ea5f33df6a533658e07866b2.png[/img]

[b]TL;DR: We'll be live streaming Learning Factory again tomorrow, April 30, 8am PST / 11am EST / 5pm CET, and you are invited! Come to our [url=https://twitch.tv/ludenio]Twitch[/url] or just check onto our Steam page at that time this Friday![/b]

Give robot a fish and... it wouldn't know what to do with it.

Teach a robot to fish - and he will feed an unlimited amount of cats for a lifetime!

That's exactly what the I.L.L.U.M.I.N.A.T.I. brightest scientists had on their minds when they were conceiving the Fishing Pier, which is now available to research and build for all KOTOVOD engineers!

Of course, there is the magnificent Fish Maker to do that work, but... It also is an advanced piece of machinery, capable of producing fish out of thin air. The oceans of Mars, on the other hand, are already full of fish-imitating edible robots, which were dropped there during the early colonization stages. They resemble real fish in every way, except for they are not real fish... still delicious though.

As KOTOVOD administration (and, subsequently, everyone else) believes, the introduction of the Fishing Peer should help saturate the demand for Fish and Cat Food during the early stages of Learning Factory building.

Science is triumphant again today! Lives are improving and the future is bright! Glory to KOTOVOD!

[*] Fish Maker machine is now placed further on the Research Tree
[*] New hotkeys available
[*] Slots in the Store can be emptied with one click
[*] UI improved
[*] Bugs fixed

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #26: Terraforming, Hoverboarding, Map Generating!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/5828d44c06900bb46c24f5cefefe828d204e0ce3.png[/img]
It all started with a small rover. 

Then, a bunch of other rovers joined the party.

Things have gone wild when Cat Warmth Amplifiers started turning feline cuteness energy for warming up Mars and bringing Earth-like atmosphere to the Red planet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/3e40513adce10b3c1cd63345fc4ff0a10b76b7a6.png[/img]

This process took time and KOTOVOD engineers were stuck on a small patch of land, building tiny factories for producing small parties of next generation goods for cats.

But today, we're going BIG! As Cat Warmth Amplifiers are operating at full capacity, Mars is now open for exploration, with thousands of square kilometers of land to be discovered and conquered, and turned into paradise for both humans and cats (mostly for cats though).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/6be64da0bf7ac26089dfaf2b25996abc146354a5.png[/img]

KOTOVOD engineers, as usual, are riding the crest of the wave of progress: all thanks to the new hoverboards, conceived at the I.L.L.U.M.I.N.A.T.I. headquarters. They are meant to skyrocket the productivity rates at Learning Factories. Although not tested for safety, they're guaranteed to ensure the safety of all cats riding them - all thanks to the living safety bag in the form of a meat bag which is a human engineer.

The future looks bright for KOTOVOD and the feline race! So let's rejoice for the moment and then get back to hard work. Or else!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/060598df0fda615a54ea05a328223e69c07a2e30.png[/img]

[h2]Version 0.9.19 Released[/h2]
[h3]New Game Mode: Freeplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] In this mode you're free to build your map without having to go through all the tutorials. But most importantly, you can fine tune your map using Map Generation Tool
[/list]
[h3]Procedural Map generation[/h3]
[list]
[*] There's now a mini-map (and a maxi-map) for easier navigation
[*] Choose your map size: from 256*256 to glorious 512*512 tiles
[*] Choose land coverage: from a huge continent to a tiny island
[*] Choose land density: from one huge chunk of soil to an archipelago of islands
[*] Choose land sharpness: from smooth to extra sharp shorelines
[*] Choose land centralization: do you want more land in the center of the map, or maybe you would like to see some water there
[*] New mechanics: Fertility. Soil (and water - reserved for future updates) can now be either fertile or infertile. Infertile soil spawns trees (regular and fir) and metal sources, fertile soils spawn Apple Trees and Cotton Plants. Those latter plants can be planted into infertile soil (see "Terraforming" section below), but will grow and multiply at a slower rate. If a plant is fully grown, not being harvested and has no place to multiply, it can increase the fertility of the tile under it (but cannot change the type of soil) for future plants
[*] You can fine tune coverage, density and border sharpness of fertile/infertile soil in the editor, too
[*] In the "Map details" section you can also tune coverage and density for resource types. Please note that metal/trees and cotton/apples are interconnected: in any of these pairs, both parameters can't be set to 100% simultaneously
[*] "Randomize Seed" function allows you to create a whole new map using the same parameters you've selected
[*] Finally, copy and paste the key from "Map Key" section and send it to your friends, so they could play the game on that same map
[/list]
[h3]Hoverboard[/h3]
[list]
[*] As seen in the movies! Reasearch it in the Monument and then press and hold "Shift" to glide around the factory like it's going out of style! Cannot glide over the water though (as seen in some movies, too)
[/list]
[h3]Terraforming[/h3]
[list]
[*] Research and use our brand new Shovel tool to lift tiles of map, take them somewhere else and replace some other tiles
[*] You can now pull growing plants and trees from the ground and plant them elsewhere
[*] Growing plants, water and soil can also be researched and crafted
[*] Other Gameplay Changes
[*] Turing Trees and Apple Trees can now be harvested for wood
[*] Storage units can now store up to 40 items (grouped by quantities of up to 10)
[*] New structure: Vertical Cable allows laying Optic Cables under the ground
[*] Research Labs can now research stuff even without data from connected Stores, but they will do so at 25% of their normal speed
[*] Research tree re-balanced
[*] Resource harvesting re-balanced
[/list]
[h3]Interface[/h3]
[list]
[*] Available buildings and researches are now divided into categories; in addition to standard categories, you can also assign buildings and structures to your Favorites list
[*] Check out what's currently inside a Splitter/Tunnel by hovering your mouse over them
[*] The amount of an item picked from the ground is now visible
[*] The amount of items on a Storage is now visible
[*] Some keys from the mouse can be accessed from keyboard as well
[*] Tutorials updated
[/list]
[h3]Graphics[/h3]
[list]
[*] New tiles for the map (obviously)
[*] Cat Sharpeners are now animated
[*] New character design (cat included!)
[*] New icons for certain items
[/list]
[h3]Misc[/h3]
[list]
[*] Interface optimization
[*] Performance optimization
[*] Bug fixes
[*] 5 new achievements
[/list]

[h3]NB: Due to many structural changes to the game, saved game files from the previous versions won't work anymore. We're very sorry about that
[/h3]

notes.title: Status Report: Tile Maps + Freeplay Mode + Drill-Riding Cat (Maybe)
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/6de4a3a2bb08365be6892cd382cd16d10dcfc050.jpg[/img]
Ahoy, engineers!

As you have probably guessed by the picture, the next content update of Learning Factory is not ready yet. 

It's not because we're lazy (we've got cats to be lazy for us), but because that update is probably gonna be [b]massive[/b]. 

You see, we were planning to make tile generated maps. But then we thought: what's the point of making procedurally generated maps without Freeplay Mode? 

So, now we're making that Freeplay Mode, too.

As for the maps, here's how they look in the current version (any Dwarf Fortress fans here?):

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/4f8c595c971a53218fc1f46387c236e4be92d7a7.png[/img]

That's because our artist is still working on procedurally generated landscape art. It's not in the game yet, but it looks mesmerizing already:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/eba7567771d64bd141ac03dabb7d59a8ac477ed7.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/6af254fadcedebbefc17a703eb6baf21145aa0b6.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/70581f110c2244f53c225c038af89d49c84d19a7.jpg[/img]

In case you'd like to go into technical details, those landscapes are generated with Blender's geometry nodes feature. Here's how the algorithm looks (any while True: learn() fans here?):

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/c421c4940224d24591f08248db2951c43d331292.jpg[/img]

So as you can see, we've been busy! Unfortunately, we still can't put a release date on that very peculiar update. Fingers crossed, we're expecting it to come out in 2-3 weeks. We'll keep you posted!

In other news: a working chat joke has gone too far and generated this image of a Drill-Riding Cat. Please don't ask us how did we come to this. That was not supposed to have happened. Nobody asked our artist to draw it, but he did anyway:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/771dace58a4c99f570f63fd035a21cd6a49a2e28.gif[/img]

We don't have plans for implementing this beautiful creature into the game just yet, but if you insist, you're very welcome to [url=https://discord.gg/xgvYqWf][b]go to our Discord sever and upvote it into existence[/b][/url]!

That's it for today! Follow the updates, greatness awaits! Glory to science! Glory to KOTOVOD!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/e03b95522e9090927818e77466d05cd9c2a11ed4.jpg[/img]

Greetings, comrade engineers!

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #23: New Cat Breed, New Machinery And More
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/a27b69ae0314a50cbe740aab2b39ca8e2a388542.png[/img]
It's been merely a week since KOTOVOD Learning Factory has re-opened its doors to general public, but the fruits of hard work are already in bloom, and boy, are they promising! Cats of all kinds are visiting the factory these days: including a very peculiar breed of Clerk Cats, who are usually too busy with work to be shopping (nice try though: we all know that cats are only pretending to be working)! But they have made an exception due to how awesome the KOTOVOD goods are! Especially with the brand new Loom machine, that is making the finest pieces of cloth for cat Pillows.

The Factory's administration has also recommended us to remind all the engineers: please don't mind the machinery malfunctions at the moment, our tech staff is working hard on fixing those. There's no immanent danger to the personnel. Maybe. We'll figure this out. Please follow the updates.

[h2]Version 0.8.16 Released[/h2]
[list]
[*] New breed of cats - Clerk Cats
[*] New Building: Loom; New Resource - Cloth (required for producing Pillows)
[*] If two tiles of Transporters are facing each other, items don't move on them
[*] After connecting an ML Model to a Store, prices are set by a Model by default
[*] Prices suggested by an ML model are now visible in the price table
[*] Player can no longer set prices for goods that cannot be purchased in a Store
[*] A new Iron Vein is added to the map (available after starting a new game)
[*] Passing through Cotton fields and Trees made easier
[*] The game saves automatically each 15 minutes and upon closing the game
[*] Stores' inventory increased (delete and replace existing Stores for the change to take effect)
[*] Traveling between map levels made easier
[*] A new and useful type of events added
[*] Tutorial updates
[*] UI updates
[*] Bug fixes
[/list]

Until next time! Glory to science! Glory to KOTOVOD!

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #19: We Need More Data
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/c1c46ba35db45101f033e925a76e3b74ece08293.png[/img]
An average KOTOVOD engineer is known to be capable of fixing a synchrophasotron with a pen and some duct tape. These kind of skills are very vital, since the Union-era equipment on KOTOVOD sometimes used to break even before it was put into production.

However, after making some careful calculations, the Factory administration decided that wasting resources of creative minds on fixing holes must come to an end. Which is why they have upgraded KOTOVOD's operational systems. Now they're capable of tracking sales data in real time, allowing engineers to save time on staring at the numbers for hours. And that's not just it! A set of comfort-improving measures was taken, and according to our in-house non-anonymous mandatory survey, over 147% of engineers are completely satisfied with their working experience.

[h2]Version 0.7.13 Released[/h2]
[list]
[*] Event notification system: the game now informs the player of important events, such as new cats attending the factory or new kinds of goods in high demand
[*] Lumber Mill is now animated
[*] New cat features added
[*] Improved starting map
[*] Sphinx is now dug up instantly, along with the Lab
[*] When gathering multiple resources from the map at once, the kinds of resources made more distinguishable
[*] Added a tip for buildings that can be rotated
[*] Crafting window can now be opened separately (use 'C' button)
[*] In-game wiki can now be accessed only after digging up the monument
[*] New pipette tool: press 'Q' to instantly pick a selected building, if you have it crafted
[*] Entrances and exits from the buildings are now displayed in different colors
[*] Player character can move between the buildings placed next to each other
[*] Items can be dragged between windows
[*] Items from the building panel can also be dragged
[*] Minor UI/UX improvements
[*] Bug fixes
[*] Optimization, mainly of save loading time: it now happens twice as faster in certain cases
[/list]

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #18: Rolling Into the Future
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/791a871b81e133f726399b096de0e420a0224d71.png[/img]
Happy Holidays, everyone!

KOTOVOD engineers do not have holidays, however, because cats have needs 7 days a week, 365 days a year (or rather, 687 of your Earth days, because a year on Mars lasts longer). This is why our scientists have released a major performance improvement update to the Learning Factory's apparatus and machinery right before the New Year: so we all could gladly start achieving even bolder goals right from the start of 2021!

Please return to the work ASAP before you get declared a slacker!

But we know how to have fun, too: many cats, visiting KOTOVOD Learning Factory these days, are wearing festive outfits to cheer up our workers. It's the small things that make up the atmosphere, you know, not those useless celebrations and days off! 

Happy New Year! See you on the factory real soon. Brace yourself for a year of hard work:

[h3]Learning Factory goes to Early Access in Q1 2021[/h3]

Until next time, engineers!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/4f70fb8ce7da0ab2ec2e01eeae4757f5191816f7.gif[/img]

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #17: The Wonders of Science
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/7b279c517f81273e54c0750482271479c405fb71.png[/img]
The way of KOTOVOD engineer is a pioneer's way, the one paving the glorious way to cats and humanity through uncharted stars... Alas, sometimes this path has obstacles on it, and one can't follow it without tripping over them once in a while. 

But what lies in the end makes it all worthwile! This week, for example, KOTOVOD workers are celebrating the introduction of a new, improved version of Linear Regression machine - Polynomial Regression is reporting for duty to predict optimal prices for the best cat goods even better!

This phenomenal piece of news attracted fancy-looking cats to the Factory's stores. Unfortunately, the coolness levels of these cats, combined, caused distortions in the field of visibility, effectively rendering their fancy hats, canes and monocles invisible to a living person's eye. So these cats can only be recognized by their snobbish posture. But our technicians are already working on ways to fixing this unfortunate physical effect. Please stay tuned for further updates!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/47e530218e59c26ca0d0bb4e99b59e9b7a5f01e2.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] New machine learning model added to the game: enter the Polynomial Regression - a more sophisticated version of good ol' Linear Regression
[*] Three new features are being processed by ML models: cats' headwear, equipped item and accessories are taken into account when predicting the optimal price. These features are processed using [url=https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/machinelearning/big-learning-made-easy-with-counts]Counters[/url] [b]NB:[/b] Unfortunately, we are yet to add art for said items, which will happen in one of the next updates. As of today, they're all invisible. But they're there!
[*] Cat generation reworked: cats now have hidden features (see above), they can also order multiple item types at once
[*] Lots of minor fixes in UX/UI

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #16: In Robots We Trust
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/0698eb7fa363da032082caca9f51e5df88bc46f6.png[/img]
Not all heroes wear capes. Come to think of it, not all of them wear clothes at all. Our robots usually wear no clothes (doing it with pride, too), but their part in building a better future for cats and humans is a very important one! It is our Cat Store Brobot Sales Managers, our Data Storages and Linear Regression machines that make KOTOVOD tick and collect and process data to fuel our very improtant research. And this week, their firmware has gone through a major update to ensure top notch performance on their never-ending duty! 

On the other hand, our cat scientists surprisingly wear clothes at times, but their work is even more important and heroic. It was them who were living days with all work and no play with their favorite yarn balls, to make sure this data science breakthrough was even possible. Eternal glory to their heroic deeds!

And then, there are also human engineers, building all that stuff, planning, collecting resources, establishing production chains and doing other less fancy, but also kinda important work. You guys are ok, too.

Glory to science! Glory to KOTOVOD!

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #15: Warp and Peace
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/6df9cb02eae1179dab2ae7b1b1ec1219a2a50572.png[/img]

KOTOVOD is not just a factory to make cats happier (although most time it's exactly what it is): it is also a hub of knowledge about cats and machine learning! That is why, starting from today, a comprehensive wiki is available to all Learning Factory engineers. In that wiki, you will find all the basic information about how machine learning is applied in the game and in real life back on Earth.

That knowledge will come in very handy, as more and more cats are flowing into Cat Stores through the renewed Cat Gates. Where do they come from? We might never know. Who created that Gate? We sure do know how to make it even bigger, because cats deserve to be living in abundance and to start living like that, they need to visit KOTOVOD and stuff, specifically engineered and designed to make them happy! notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #14: On the Edge of the Luxury Era
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/eec345c4a3d851f301aece0280f98a2e8de661f8.png[/img]
Everyone knows that felines and humans have had darker pages in their mutual history. Sometimes it was about some tiger occasionally munching on some expendable human. But most frequently it were the humans who were harassing defenceless cats for looking too suspicious.

Fortunately, these grim times are over now. Even more fortunately, humans are now aware that although cats do not possess any kind of magic (which, honestly, would be kinda cool) they do carry around their infinite wisdom. And thanks to the magic of science, humans can make it up for centuries of kicking cats around. The time of KOTOVOD has come!

This week brings at least one more impressive piece of machinery to make your cats feel special: meet the glorious Pillow Maker, which, perhaps not surprisingly, produces pillows of exquisite quality to roll on. In order to make sure that there's enough cloth for making these luxurious items, Cotton Collectors have been redesigned for more efficient production.

Luxury stock attracts luxurious customers: rich and elite cats have been spotted on Learning Factory campus, looking (and finding!) the most extravagant and fashionable goods. And this is but the beginning! Thanks to the work of KOTOVOD engineers, cats will thrive in abundance!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/36ddbbea6e6e7edd8a726d0a53f11e958c1b2161.jpg[/img]

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #13: Fruits of Hard Work
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/774e6c93f58376ee6ced1e7dd714fdbbf1badf57.png[/img]
On the vast planes of Mars, the harvest season never ends! Especially when it comes to harvesting fruits of hard work, being done by workers of KOTOVOD Learning Factory campus. Although the key to success is hard work around the clock, an experienced manager knows that changing even the smallest detail can sometimes lead to greatest changes.

This fall, thanks to technical modifications suggested by KOTOVOD Optimization Dept., Cotton Pickers are picking cotton from a wider territory than before: not only it boosts production, but helps fighting with excessive reforestation problem, so common on Mars these days. And that's just one of the many improvements, successfully implemented after suggestions from Optimization Dept., where work never stops, day or night. Is this department run by robots? Or maybe there are genetically modified I.L.L.U.M.I.N.A.T.I. operatives at work there? The answer is: it is not impossible! Anyway, the results are exceeding expectations and it's all that matters!

[h2]Version 0.7.7 Released[/h2]
[list]
[*] Wires visually better connect to buildings
[*] Tunnel movement direction can be reversed by clicking on it. Therefore, there's no more need to switch map layers to place some tunnels
[*] Reworked Cotton Picker is harvesting wider areas of cotton fields, cotton can be harvested again after a certain period of time
[*] Apple Pickers now require boxes from Box Makers to be able to pack apples into boxes. Additionally, apples are also being gathered from a 3x3 tiles area
[*] New hotkeys available: [i]Ctrl+click[/i] switches between open inventory windows, [i]Shift+click[/i] picks half of a stack of an item. [i]Shift+Ctrl+Click[/i] sends half a stack of an item between open inventory windows
[*] You can drop items to buildings from your inventory without opening a building interface
[*] There's now a research progress bar for current research
[*] There's now a field for entering promo codes in the main menu. Try one of these below and see what happens: CATBUS, CHESHIRE, IRON_CAT. Also, you can get an extra one for [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd00euY--wlLAjn1qFqz7cNELwL77hKje4OCn4NrddKiFUw2g/viewform?entry.416926324=STEAM_WEB_POST]sharing your feedback here[/url] :)

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #10: Splitter Cell
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/1bcae813e2ac52d3116db04028671f88b2a7cd1b.png[/img]

[b]UPDATE:[/b] v0.7.4 is out!

[i][b]Important Notice:[/b] Due to the factor that we like to call "Stupid Humans", the release of the update is postponed [b]until Friday morning[/b]. We'll let you know as soon as it's out, stay tuned and don't forget to pet your cat on a regular basis[/i]

It is well known that the Union's engineers designed KOTOVOD machinery with perfection. When there is cats of the world happiness at stake, every mechanism must work like clockwork, period. However, when you're reaching for the stars, there's always room for improvement.

Take transporter splitters, for example! Despite working perfectly fine, previously they have only been capable of splitting stuff on conveyor lines horizontally. But now, thanks to the work of brilliant minds of KOTOVOD's scientific department, all engineers get splitters that can be rotated to split lines vertically as well!

notes.title: Learning Factory Quick Pitch
notes.content:
Hello! Thanks for stopping by. Oleg from [url=https://luden.io/]Luden.io[/url] here. We are an indie studio focused on educational video games. 

[code]If you have no time to read, here is the quick pitch - this game is about factory automation, machine learning, and cats. If you love tech - probably you should give it a shot. Sign up for Free Alpha via [url=https://discord.com/invite/uScvRYS]Discord[/url] and [b]Add to your wishlist[/b].[/code]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/b4e5264a94877eef49843002a589bdc1eea8b7b5.gif[/img]

[h2]Previously on Edu Games[/h2]
We were lucky enough to spark the curiosity about Machine Learning tech with our previous game while True: learn(). More than 20,000 students were asked by teachers to play the game in classes. Some of our players even got hired as machine learning specialists!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/619150/while_True_learn/

The story is quite funny (here is [url=https://blog.luden.io/while-true-learn-release-or-the-story-about-1-year-of-weekly-updates-machine-learning-and-cats-4ad1884e5d8e]a blog post[/url]) because we didn't expect that there is someone else like us, who like really complicated stuff like machine learning in video games. But now we know that there are a lot of us here on Steam. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/bb0226757275b7de86a9e19146fe609032781982.jpg[/img]

[h2]And now[/h2]
We decided to analyze all limitations we faced during the design of while True: learn(). A lot of them we created because of me personally, at the beginning I was too afraid to design too complicated game.

So long story short, we came up with an idea. How about taking all we love about complicated system-design games like Factorio and Rimworld and all things we love about Machine Learning? And Cats of course. 

So we design a new game to help people get familiar with Machine Learning, for those who interested in tech, who want to learn something new with their kids or students while having fun.

[h2]Welcome[/h2]
This Steam Game Festival demo is ready for you! We've spent the last 6 months combining real machine learning tech with automation gameplay and cats images and we hope you'll enjoy the game. 

[h2]How to get more involved[/h2] 
We are doing daily highlights in [url=https://twitter.com/learningfact0ry]Twitter[/url], weekly updates here on Steam, and in [url=https://discord.com/invite/uScvRYS]Discord[/url], surveys, and other fun events. You are always welcome to join us on this nerdy adventure. 

Please share feedback here on Steam or via [url=https://discord.com/invite/uScvRYS]Discord[/url], [url=https://twitter.com/learningfact0ry]Twitter[/url], by email, send us an owl, post a meme... everything works. Your feedback is the most useful and motivational thing for us!

Also if you have something confidential please feel free to contact me directly by email oleg.chumakov@luden.io. I am always happy to help!

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #6: Linear Regression and UI Upgrades
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/deb5ea02612f9df2ee28544e48ceb1cedaf1a4de.png[/img]

[b]UPDATE:[/b] v0.6.5 is officially live! Feel free to update ASAP

[b]NOTA BENE: [/b] [i]Our specialists were working their [strike]paws[/strike] hands off to prepare this update. Alas, 10 minutes before we were to release it, our machine learning machine has broken unexpectedly. Our game is promised to feature real machine learning, so we decided to postpone the next update until we truly nail it. This update will be released as soon as reasonably possible. Stay tuned. Glory to KOTOVOD![/i]

The mission of KOTOVOD Learning Factory is as simple as it is noble: to generate happiness! Happiness for both humans and cats (well, mostly for cats, because they have paws for hands and are undeniably cute). Although our brave engineers are working days and nights pursuing this dream, they are barely humans. 

«[i]Hoomanz ar veri fine for makink katz happy but hoomanz are maed of meat and fat and dont haev fur and also oftenz stoopid. No oofeanz to hoomanz, i iz a hooman mysealf so i know. Iz why hoomanz invented robots and AI machines that arez betterz for makink katz happy. Also i iz a hooman and not a kat, did i tellz you dat olready?[/i]», — Dr. Katz, a human person and KOTOVOD’s chief scientist

Competent as they are, humans are imperfect. But they are perfectly capable of dreaming and inventing machines that will help achieve those dreams! And this is what this week’s big feature is all about: all cat stores are now powered by linear regression! 

Yes, you have read it right. «KOTOVOD Worker» has mentioned this upcoming feature more than once, but this time it’s finally here to start changing lives! Each engineer is now free to turn on [b]linear regression algorithm[/b] in their Smart Cat Stores and watch as the computers are calculating the optimal price for cat goods! Glory to science! Glory to KOTOVOD!

Of course, for the time being it is but an option: prices can still be changed by engineers’ firm (and furless) hands. But could their choices be more accurate and weighed than those made by machine learning algorithms? Only time will tell! 

(Although the answer is, obviously, a «no»)

notes.title: Share Your Opinion: Learning Machine Learning With Style!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/c1f5082c64a7420be57a6fb564a997110610125e.jpg[/img]

KOTVOD needs YOU, engineer!

Yes, you! As you probably have heard already, the purpose of our glorious Learning Factory is to explain some basics of machine learning in a stylish graphic way, so even stupid humans would understand it (cats already know all there's to know about it). 

If you don't know this yet, don't hesitate to check out [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1150090/announcements/detail/4582931987115338682][b]our team's lead coder interview[/b][/url] form a couple of weeks ago

One of ML techinques that will empower your Factory will be Linear Regression. So we've made a linear regression machine so you could learn about machine learning while machines learn to learn... Ok, that came off pretty complicated, so, with no further ado, please welcome our [b]MACHINE LEARNING MACHINE[/b] for linear regression:

[h3][b]Option 1[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/c538bff674800f541ecd192069a3f1f7c64f47e0.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Option 2[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/f85c69a07227f324ae6ebb4d2fdb4211f2de4126.gif[/img]

If you have no idea of how it works and what it does, don't you worry. For now all we need from you is to let us know, which one you like more. 

[h3]Do rush to the #learing-factory room on our [url=https://discord.gg/xgvYqWf][b]Discord server[/b][/url] and vote today![/h3]

And if you want to get some background first, here's an excerpt from a [url=https://vas3k.com/blog/machine_learning/#scroll80]very comprehensive article[/url] about machine learning:

[i]"Regression is basically classification where we forecast a number instead of category. Examples are car price by its mileage, traffic by time of the day, demand volume by growth of the company etc. Regression is perfect when something depends on time.

Everyone who works with finance and analysis loves regression. It's even built-in to Excel. And it's super smooth inside — the machine simply tries to draw a line that indicates average correlation. Though, unlike a person with a pen and a whiteboard, machine does so with mathematical accuracy, calculating the average interval to every dot."[/i]

If you have time, go give this article a read, it really is awesome. Or look it up on [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_regression]Wikipedia[/url], if you're brave enough! And then come back to our [url=https://discord.gg/xgvYqWf][b]Discord server[/b][/url] and vote for the ML Machine design you find more self-explanatory!

notes.title: Happy Programmer's Day!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/6972dbbe77fb644606418dce7bd49e9ba169725d.png[/img]

Hi there! And welcome to the 256th day of the year. It is also known as "Programmer's Day" and it's a very special holiday for us. Although our latest games are not programming sims per se, they do revolve around coding. Furthermore, we believe that coders are the heroes of the XXI century, those capable of changing the world.

In other words, if you are not into coding yet, you better start catching up! And Learning Factory might be just the game for you to start with.

If you have played the alpha, you might have noticed that Learning Factory is not just about building a factory: it's about understanding and predicting the wishes of your customers, the cats. Although the concept of cats buying stuff at some factory might seem a little abstract if not absurd (to put it mildly), it is based on real-life research methods. In this post we'll try and shed some light on how we (and you!) will be using actual, real-life machine learning in this game. 

[b]Ivan Kapranov[/b], our team's own lead coder, holds a bachelor's degree in machine learning. Even more so, he's teaching it to high school students. To commemorate Programmer's Day, we've asked Ivan to shed some light on the learning part behind the Learning Factory.

[i][b]DISCLAIMER:[/b] We do understand that machine learning and coding are closely related, yet they are not the same things. Our game is specifically about the latter. If you want to learn more about coding by playing video games, please feel free to check out respective games, such as Human Resource Machine or any of Zachtronics' games. They're awesome![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/3e57898c1a7604f3fdab085d705fe5808170e94f.jpg[/img]

"We're planning to introduce several algorithms of machine learning into the game. The one I'm working on right now is linear regression that will help predicting prices for goods in the game's stores. Each of them is selling several items which can be purchased by cats. Naturally, the store's mission is to maximize the profit. Linear regression can help it a great deal. A player's main goal is to provide data (in general, the more -- the better, but it's not really that simple) to be processed by the algorithm so it could calculate the optimal price for each type of product within the data provided. E.g. if the data is of good quality, the price will be close enough to optimum, if the data is bad -- you'll get apples vs. oranges.

What kinds of features will we have in the game? For starters there will be a rather simple regression based on a few simple features, but the price predicted by such an algorithm will be far from optimum, because each cat is different and is willing to pay a certain price. Therefore a player will need to add additional features to the algorithm. We will also have sales, special offers and such… Also we plan to make different kinds of cats. Some of them might be first time customers, some would be returning. Some of them might be holding loyalty cards. Or maybe discount coupons! In order to make a factory efficient and profitable, one would have to take all these factors (and more!) into consideration.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/d18cf1581911dbbe10b9b166050bfe35358407f2.jpg[/img]

This is where linear regression does its magic. In theory, it's possible to calculate the optimal price by hand, especially if you don't mind spending a couple of days collecting and analysing data. And even after that you'd have to change the price every couple of minutes, because the circumstances are constantly changing. Is there a new president elected on Mars? Or maybe there's a problem with the supply chain of a famous cheese from Venus? Every global or local event might change the demand for goods. If you have a well tuned algorithm, it will adapt to these changes real fast by analyzing new kinds of data. (Or so we expect, because the data we're using is really simple, but we still are in the early stages of development)

Machine learning helps to take all the factors into consideration. But before that would become possible, a player would have to prepare raw data for the algorithm. Actually, this is what 95% of working with machine learning in production is all about. In Learning Factory, we are trying to make this process as graphic and illustrative as possible -- hence the factory building concept. Different kinds of buildings would collect different kinds of data, which then flows to data cluster cores where the mathematical magic is happening. Say, a player wants to build a model which would acknowledge the price of goods, the type of store and something less obvious, like, cats' ears shape. They would have to streamline the data to a cluster core, push a button and let the algorithm calculate the optimum price within the dataset.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/b7118ebff994051ff7adf824fed100d94cbcc1c6.jpg[/img]

This concludes the first iteration of machine learning, but then there's an option to go deeper and actually experiment. This is where a player will be working with regularizations that help algorithms learn better, to put it simple. They would have to learn about weights of features and how they influence the price prediction quality.

And then a player can go even deeper. We plan to introduce special kinds of buildings that will allow players to experiment with data -- multiply additional features, for example. Or exponentiation! Say, a player wants to check out what happens if an algorithm calculates the squared price of a type of goods. Maybe this way it will be more efficient. Or maybe not -- it is an experiment, after all! Another way to improve the quality of prediction is to input additional features into the model, which would also require building a certain facility in a factory.
 
The mission of Learning Factory as we see it is to illustrate linear regression (and maybe other kinds of machine learning, stay tuned for updates!) in a fun way. If you apply conservative approach to learning, you'd have to listen to several hours of lectures, then install Python and certain libraries and spend another handful of hours on coding… That is, if you have the necessary knowledge in maths and know how to write a code. The game allows you to skip all the hard stuff and still be able to grasp the general context. We want to make Learning Factory as flexible for the players as possible: you don't have to go too deep into machine learning to make your factory profitable, but those who choose to do so will discover a whole new layer of gameplay to experiment with. And if you want to dive deeper into machine learning context… well, let's just say, we have some ideas on how to bring the game closer to real life! But we'll talk about it when it's time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/bb28e915a535ab3408d10c0f0232716874202ead.jpg[/img]

We are bold enough to believe that a good video game can be a perfect supplementary material to lectures on YouTube or Coursera. And this time, things are real! Our previous game while True: learn() was merely simulating machine learning at most times, but Learning Factory will actually feature living and breathing ML algorithms for a player to experiment with. It won't make you into a real data scientist, but it can be your first step to becoming one!

In a traditional learning model, a contact with audience is very important: old school lecturing implies face to face contact, and that does not really transit into online mode. If one's trying to learn something online, it requires a very high level of inner motivation. Video games, on the other hand, are self motivating, because they're fun! And if a player absorbs some 10% of new information just by playing a game, I believe our job as developers and educators is well done!"

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/b74af9b3bbe0a71d26ae4e62a96d38b2507797d1.png[/img]
What cats really want? Why do they moan in front of a closed door but immediately lose interest in it once it's open? Why would they sometimes burst into sudden rage, destroying furniture and wallpapers all over the place? We don't know all the answers, but science has just come one step closer to finding it out! Alas, it now seems to be facing a closed door. Dr. Katz, chief scientific officer of KOTOVOD Cat Learning Factory, sent out this message announcing a brand new type of research facilities -- the Clusters.

[i]"We haev built kluster corez to collect oll kindz of data about catz. Sadly, wes dont haev dataz to analyze yet. But someday we willz. What a tiem to be aliv!"[/i]

What a time indeed! Someday, cluster cores will become the main interface for operating with data from various cat facilities of the factory. But for now they are available for every KOTOVOD engineer to build and admire. Apparently, that's all they do at the moment. The Factory's scientists also claim that watching those cores for prolonged periods of time is great for soothing nerves. Rumors about them being able to damage one's retina are just silly rumors, according to our brightest minds. Still, HR department required us to mention that corporate health insurance policy does not cover damage from watching cluster cores. Or any damage, actually. 

In other news, please try not to miss the next special issue of KOTOVOD Worker, dedicated to this year's Programmers Day. Our scientists are planning to shed some lights about how clusters process the data about cats.

notes.title: KOTOVOD Worker #1: First Playable Alpha Available
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/990bdce60e4436163c51e8588e9ecc30462a40d7.png[/img]

Chief operating engineer Ivan is looking smart and humbled, wearing a suit and a smile. And yet, he cannot hide his inner shining of pride. At last, his professional love child, the mighty KOTOVOD, is re-opening its doors! It has been closed for decades, with cats all over the world left idle and misunderstood by their human companions. Well, this era of frustration is coming to an end!

The KOTOVOD was conceived and constructed back in the socialist era. The scientists of that time have had a theory that cats were actually sentient beings, which brought them to creating an ambitious project: a scientific factory which would help humans understand what their cats really want and what they have to say.

After the Union collapsed, the factory fell into oblivion. But thanks to cutting edge technology, humanity was given a second chance to finally find a common tongue with their furry friends! Old machines are empowered by modern science: cats’ needs and desires are analysed by a complicated machine learning algorithm that helps build a better factory for a brighter feline future. 

Chief scientific officer, Dr. Katz, was not available for an interview, being heads down busy with his scientific endeavours in his office. He did send a short note to commemorate the glorious day: [i]«Iz going az planned. Iz going good. Sorry kant haz interviewz, very bizi doing reserch wit my hooman fingerz (not cat paws haha). Kalculating very stronk. Oh, iz that a mouze?..»[/i]

[h2]Learning Factory: Alpha Is Live![/h2]

Chief engineer Ivan, on the other hand, was more than glad to elaborate on his hard work:

[i]«Today we are about to launch the next module of the factory into action. Am I worried? Of course not, we're professionals! Besides, it's an alpha-version, so something definitely might go wring. Like that infamous case with canned food... poor Vlad has been having nightmares ever since, his body hair turned purple, what a mess... Oh well! We are running accident-free for almost 3 days now and I have a good feeling about this one!»[/i]

An admirable optimism of a true engineer! We were authorized by KOTOVOD's administration to publish a list of vital new features, available at the factory in this alpha-version:

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] Players can now build multiple cat shops at their factories
[*] Refined shops' mechanics: 4 goods can be sold simultaneously in each shop, with an option to assign individual price for each goods type
[*] Introducing the Research Tree
[*] Certain resource types (money, raw data, data features and articles) are now displayed in virtual format and no longer appear as objects on the game's map
[*] Introducing optical fibers that will help join certain production chains into clusters. [b]NB[/b]: they don't actually work in this first version, but they still look neat
[*] New cat generating algorithm ([b]NB[/b]: again, not very functional yet, but pretty)
[*] Each building now has a different demolishing time. That said, one won't be able to accidentally destroy a brand new show with one click anymore, and deleting useless transporter tiles is faster and easier than ever before
[*] Destroying element sources (such as piles of iron or apple trees) now gives a larger amount of respective elements
[/list]

[h3]Interface & Graphics[/h3]
[list]
[*] UI has been reworked in many ways. Still, there are a lot of placeholder items at this stage, so if something is not working, then maybe it's not supposed to, yet
[*] Crafting queue is now available in the inventory
[*] Quick saving the game with a 'Ctrl+S' keyboard shortcut is now available
[*] New and improved hot keys: press 'T' to open the Research Tree or use 'Esc' to close all windows
[*] The first animated piece of machinery: basic manipulator is now capable of visually manipulating objects:
[/list]

[h2]How to Join?[/h2]
KOTOVOD is hiring! The corridors of KOTOVOD are humming with power once again, yet there’s so much more to do! We need more engineers to fine tune and test our catting-edge technologies.

notes.title: Meet Learning Factory
notes.content:
Hello! Thanks for stopping by. Oleg from [url=https://luden.io/]Luden.io[/url] here. We are an indie studio focused on educational video games. 

[code]If you have no time to read, here is the short pitch - this game is about factory automation, machine learning, and cats. If you love tech - probably you should give it a shot. Free Alpha coming soon, you can sign up via [url=https://discord.com/invite/uScvRYS]Discord[/url] or [url=https://nivalvr.us11.list-manage.com/subscribe/post?u=524b2f0bfc899ad323e62bcf3&id=3d62d2eebd]by email[/url].[/code]

[h2]Previously on Edu Games[/h2]
We were lucky enough to spark the curiosity about Machine Learning tech with our previous game while True: learn(). More than 20,000 students were asked by teachers to play the game in classes. Some of our players even got hired as machine learning specialists!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/619150/while_True_learn/

The story is quite funny (here is [url=https://blog.luden.io/while-true-learn-release-or-the-story-about-1-year-of-weekly-updates-machine-learning-and-cats-4ad1884e5d8e]a blog post[/url]) because we didn't expect that there is someone else like us, who like really complicated stuff like machine learning in video games. But now we know that there are a lot of us here on Steam. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38078557/4c96511aa4a598ca20baf5b2240fb0295cf03e37.jpg[/img]

[h2]And now[/h2]
That's why we decided to analyze all limitations we faced during the design of while True: learn(). A lot of them we created because of me personally, because at the beginning I was too afraid to design too complicated game.

So long story short, we came up with an idea. How about taking all we love about complicated system-design games like Factorio and Rimworld and all things we love about Machine Learning? And Cats of course. 

So we design a new game to help people get familiar with Machine Learning, for those who interested in tech, who want to learn something new with their kids or students while having fun.
